extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, auditors, accounting and legal advisors, and other stakeholders preparing or reviewing SEC climate-related financial disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Final SEC rules and related guidance on preparing and presenting climate-related disclosures in Commission filings and financial statements, including scope, timing, audit/ICFR treatment, and special rules for different issuer types (SRCs, EGCs, foreign issuers, BDCs).

rubrics_metrics.name: ASC Topic 820 — fair value judgments disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: FASB ASC Topic 820 Fair Value Measurement requires an entity to disclose judgments and assumptions about assets and liabilities measured at fair value in the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as an existing GAAP requirement that parallels the need for transparency about assumptions used to measure items at fair value; included to show precedent for requiring disclosure of significant estimates and judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASC Topic 842 — lease assumptions disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: FASB ASC Topic 842 Leases requires lessees to disclose information about significant assumptions and judgments made in applying the requirements of Topic 842.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an example of an accounting standard that requires disclosure of significant assumptions and judgments, supporting the approach to requiring disclosure of climate-related assumptions used in financial statement preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidated-scope calculation of disclosure threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must calculate the financial-statement disclosure using financial information that is consistent with the scope of the rest of their consolidated financial statements included in the filing (i.e., not separately at parent and subsidiary levels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responds to commenter concerns about duplication/double-counting and clarifies that disclosure thresholds are evaluated on the same consolidated basis as the filing's financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal coverage for financial-statement effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure periods correspond to the financial statements required in the filing: two years of financial-statement effects corresponding to balance sheets (when two most recent fiscal year balance sheets are included) and three years of effects corresponding to income statements (when three most recent fiscal year income statements are included).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 17 CFR provisions and explains EGC and smaller reporting company (SRC) filing accommodations (e.g., EGCs may provide shorter audited periods in an IPO registration statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of climate disclosures (financial statements vs separate report)
rubrics_metrics.description: Material climate-related financial impacts should be reflected within the financial statements (including notes); some commenters suggested flexibility to place disclosures together with related disclosures rather than in a standalone climate footnote, and some supported a separate audited climate report but not as a replacement for disclosures in financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record includes differing views: some prefer inclusion in existing reports for consistency and investor access, others recommend location flexibility or a stand-alone audited climate report in addition to (not instead of) financial-statement disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit and ICFR applicability to climate disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether climate-related disclosures (including specified metrics) should be subject to audit and internal control over financial reporting (ICFR) is contested among commenters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments ranged from requiring audit and ICFR coverage to arguing against such requirements; references to PCAOB auditing standards and concerns that GAAP-level climate accounting guidance may be needed before imposing audits are cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit report preparation must be by registered public accounting firms
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unlawful for any person that is not a registered public accounting firm to prepare or issue, or to participate in the preparation or issuance of, any audit report with respect to any issuer, broker, or dealer (15 U.S.C. 7212).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited to support the expectation that the company's regular auditor will perform any required audit of climate-related metrics or disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign private issuer presentation and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign private issuers that prepare financial statements under IFRS will comply with IASB requirements for form and content within the financial statements, but Article 14 disclosure (as proposed) was required; the Commission proposed amending Part I of Form 20-F to require climate-related disclosures and explained the interactions with Forms F-1, S-3, F-3 and Form 6-K furnishing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that Form 20-F amendments make formal amendments to F-1 unnecessary, notes that Form 6-K furnishing of climate disclosures depends on General Instruction B criteria, and references prior SEC releases on foreign issuer acceptance of IFRS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business development companies (BDCs) subject to disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: BDCs (closed-end investment companies with a class of equity securities registered under or with a registration statement filed under section 12 of the Exchange Act) are required to file Exchange Act annual reports and thus subject to the climate-disclosure requirements applicable to section 12 registrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites statutory definition (section 54 of the Investment Company Act) and notes that like other section 12 registrants, BDCs file Exchange Act annual reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaled compliance accommodations for SRCs and EGCs (phase-in / exemptions / safe harbor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The record includes requests for scaled, phased, or delayed disclosures (including proposed exemptions or safe harbors) for smaller reporting companies (SRCs) and emerging growth companies (EGCs); commenters requested relief for IPOs and attenuated attestation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters recommended phase-ins or temporary safe harbors (e.g., for SRCs or EGCs), while the Commission declined or limited certain exemptions (e.g., no exemption/transition for registrants engaged in an IPO); the record contains numerous letters recommending scaled relief and specific proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure triggers tied to balance sheet and income statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules call for disclosure triggered off both the balance sheet and the income statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See discussion referencing section II.K.3.c.ii — i.e., certain disclosures are required when the financial-statement line items (balance sheet or income statement) are present for the indicated periods in the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of climate-impacted financial assumptions in notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial assumptions impacted by climate-related events and conditions should be included in the notes to the financial statements where they appropriately reflect the financial consequences of these climate factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted that financial-assumption impacts may be most appropriately disclosed alongside related financial-statement notes rather than solely in a separate climate footnote; several letter writers recommended placement flexibility to group related disclosures together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 3 emissions disclosure and exemptions debate
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether SRCs (and other smaller issuers) should be exempted from Scope 3 emissions disclosures was widely debated; many commenters opposed indefinite exemptions for SRCs from Scope 3 reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record includes letters both opposing and supporting limited/temporary safe harbors; some advocated temporary measures but urged eventual comprehensive coverage for small and large companies alike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandate to include material climate disclosures in Commission filings (vs furnishing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters recommended that the Commission require registrants to provide material climate-related disclosures in Commission filings and permit registrants to furnish additional mandated information that the registrant determines is not material in a separate climate report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ICI recommended material disclosures be required in filings while allowing registrants to furnish other mandated information in new climate reports; alternative approaches to placement and furnishing were discussed in comment letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCAOB auditing standards applicability and prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urged that the PCAOB prioritize development and adoption of auditing standards for climate-related metrics and identified existing PCAOB auditing standards (e.g., AS 1200 series, AS 2105, AS 3101) as relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters identify a suite of PCAOB standards that may be relevant to auditing such metrics and recommend PCAOB action; some commenters noted situations where auditors' risk-assessment judgments would affect scope and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditor scoping judgments and potential inefficiencies/costs
rubrics_metrics.description: There could be situations where climate-related metrics are in scope for audit while the underlying financial-statement line items ordinarily would not be, leading auditors to scope in lower-risk accounts, potentially creating significant inefficiencies and increased audit costs with minimal investor benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raised by commenters (e.g., CAQ, Baker Tilly) to caution about practical audit implications of scoping decisions and the need for careful consideration of what should be in-scope for audit and ICFR.
